newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday with most investors staying on the sidelines ahead of the Chinese lunar new year holiday, traders said.
The key March 1997 contract ended at 3,146 yuan ($379) per tonne, rising six yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 3,059 and hit a high of 3,150.
May rose 40 to 3,240, the January 1998 contract fell 10 to 3,380.
Traders said many investors took a wait-and-see attitude with the approach of the two-week holiday.
"Retail investors dominated today's trade again while institutions were not interested in trading," one trader said.
"Soybeans will not fluctuate sharply in the short term given a lack of market-moving news," he added.
